unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts two sentences that the first draft kept. One is the old man's reconsideration ('Going over the experience again, long after all the great actors were dead...'). The other is the foreshadowing 'The inevitable followed... the young man on the edge of life never dreamed.' The rupture paragraph now opens flatly on the young man's obedience.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Para 23's 'as long as life lasted' and para 24's 'then or afterwards' still imply long hindsight.

evidence.quote: Going over the experience again, long after all the great actors were dead, he struggled to see where he had blundered.
Going over the experience again, long after all the great actors were dead, he struggled to see where he had blundered.
He had necessarily followed Seward and his father; he took for granted that his business was obedience, discipline, and silence.
The inevitable followed, as a child fresh from the nursery should have had the instinct to foresee, but the young man on the edge of life never dreamed.
Rightly or wrongly the new President and his chief advisers decided that, before they could administer the Government

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 20-word 'Going over the experience again...' sentence at the head of para 22.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Not listed as essential, but supports the voice profile's old-man/young-man distinction; a planning gap.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The voice profile requires keeping the young man's beliefs distinct from the old man's later judgment. Without these markers the shock loses its ironic, long-range framing, and the chapter's turn toward its lesson arrives without the narrator's signpost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Retrospective frame around the Sumner rupture removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'Mr. Seward was never petty or personal; his talk was large...'. As a result, 'What was more unusual... he had some means' directly follows 'From the first sight, he loved the Governor', where 'he' is Henry. 'More unusual' also loses the list of virtues it is compared against. The 'too simple a nature to know' punchline on mask and nature is gone as well.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'unknown to other Senators' disambiguates by the end of the sentence. The macaw portrait, the mask-versus-features line and 'Henry Adams thought it charming' survive.

evidence.quote: He noticed that Mr. Seward was never petty or personal; his talk was large; he generalized; he never seemed to pose for statesmanship
Mr. Seward was never petty or personal; his talk was large; he did not require an attitude of prayer.
From the first sight, he loved the Governor, who, though sixty years old, had the youth of his sympathies. What was more unusual--almost singular and quite eccentric--he had some means

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert 'Mr. Seward was never petty or personal; his talk was large;' before 'What was more unusual'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required (Seward portrait, effect of unselfishness); an execution loss within a required unit.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The pronoun briefly invites misreading, and the climax of the portrait ('effect of unselfishness') loses its build-up and its paradox of a simple nature unable to tell its own mask from its features.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Seward portrait: 'he had some means' now follows a Henry-subject sentence

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept 'Of course he looked anxiously for a sign of character' and the concluding judgment: no man needed so much education, yet all he could get would not be enough. The revision cuts both. It ends on 'above all a lack of apparent force', so the misjudgment that 'would have lost' refers to is never stated as Adams's estimate.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Had young Adams been told... he would have lost' still precedes the portrait, and 'lack of apparent force' implies the judgment.

evidence.quote: Any private secretary in the least fit for his business would have thought, as Adams did, that no man living needed so much education as the new President
Of course he looked anxiously for a sign of character. He saw a long, awkward figure
the same painful sense of becoming educated and of needing education that tormented a private secretary; above all a lack of apparent force.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the final 'Any private secretary... would not be enough' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required (Lincoln judged as lacking force, flagged 'would have lost').
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The continuity check requires the Lincoln misjudgment to remain the young man's view. Without the 'as Adams did' sentence, the estimate is less clearly his, and the tie between Lincoln and the chapter's education ledger is lost.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Explicit Lincoln estimate cut; 'would have lost' frames only an image

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the line that answers the father's quiet irony: 'The young man was beyond satire, and asked only a pretext for throwing all education to the east wind.' It also cuts 'plunged at once into a lurid atmosphere of politics', which sets up the next paragraph's 'lurid'. Both were in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The father's irony itself survives intact, and the Wide-Awake paragraph keeps 'lurid beyond description'.

evidence.quote: The young man was beyond satire, and asked only a pretext for throwing all education to the east wind.
The young man was beyond satire, and asked only a pretext for throwing all education to the east wind.
as though any young man who could afford to throw away two winters on the Civil Law could afford to read Blackstone for another winter without a master.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the one 'beyond satire' sentence at the end of para 3.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required unit (father does not mock the Pandects); voice-profile loss.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The paired irony (father's hint, son's eager abandonment of education) becomes one-sided. The chapter's first tally of education thrown away is lost, and the 'lurid' echo no longer links the two paragraphs.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Son's reply to the father's irony dropped
